_doc: EATING THE DEAD IN A SIEGE (systems/eatingTheDead.js). A starving garrison (stores at nothing for at least minStarvingDays, a garrison of at least minGarrison) can eat its dead. THE DEAD counted: the garrison it has lost since the siege began, and the townsfolk dead of hunger and sickness (dead x townDeadShare). STORES: + base + dead x perDead days of food, at most max (x 0.5 a second time, never a third). THE GARRISON: morale x moraleKeep the day it starts (the horror), a sickness chance (sick: bad meat, the town's disease); the starving loss stops while it lasts. THE TOWN is never the same: settlement.ateDead { day, by, epithet } (the epithet picked from epithets: what the realms call it after), a TownMemory atrocity mark (grief x long), its happiness happiness at once, its townsfolk marked (p.ateDead: their annals) and the survivors of the garrison remember; the realm's faith frowns (faith: the town's realm's stability / your standing with that faith). WHO: the AI garrison you besiege (systems/sieges.js) does it of itself (ai.chance a day once it may, x ai.cruel with a cruel lord, x ai.noQuarter when your name says no quarter); a crown's town your commissioned host besieges (player/generalship.js) — its surrender slowed by ai.generalSlow; your own besieged holding (systems/holdingSieges.js): you order it from the siege panel (Holdings Under Siege), or forbid it — else its governor may do it on his own (governor.chance a day after governor.afterDays starving, x ai.cruel with a cruel or ruthless governor). For yours: Atrocities 'ateDead' (karma, the butcher's name a little, every realm's regard, ate_dead_heard, the chronicle, the news), faithStanding with the realm's faith, the town's loyalty (holding happiness) loyalty.

ai: Smoke rises from inside {town} at odd hours, and the men on the walls no longer look starved. Your scouts say they are eating their dead.
Deserters from {town} tell of the garrison's dead carried to the kitchens. The town will hold out longer than anyone thought.
yours: Inside {town} the garrison carries its dead to the kitchens. It will hold for {days} days more. No one who lives through it will ever eat meat again without remembering.
governor: {governor} could not watch them starve any longer: the garrison of {town} has eaten its dead. It will hold {days} days more. You were not asked.
forbid: You send word into {town}: no man is to touch the dead. They will starve with clean hands.
name: Ever after, the towns around call it {town} {epithet}.
